title: llm-session-routing-proposal-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal sketch for a session-routing layer intended to sit between the Redwood API gateway and the serving runtime. Goal is to provide deterministic session affinity, per-session config overrides (quantization, batch hints, model variant), and controlled graceful degradation when capacity is constrained.

Goals / non-goals:
- Provide sticky routing for conversations so KV cache locality is maximized (lower tail latency, better cost).
- Expose a simple per-session policy DSL to the Console and SDKs for canarying and cost controls.
- Allow transparent model-variant fallback (e.g., fp16 -> int8 -> small model) while preserving session continuity where possible.
- NOT a full load balancer replacement; keep it lightweight and shard-aware.

Constraints / assumptions:
- We assume runtime instances can accept a session token header and will read/write a shared KV cache (or have local cache warmed by the same session routing decisions).
- Sessions have a lifetime (TTL) configured by the caller or derived from activity.
- Multi-region routing should favor region-local instances unless policy requires global routing.

High-level flow (text diagram):

Client SDK/HTTP -> API Gateway (auth) -> Session Router -> Serving Runtime Pool -> Model Instance
                                |
                                +-> Session store (redis/consul) for affinity metadata and KPIs

Router responsibilities (bullet):
- Create / attach / detach sessions
- Maintain session metadata: model_variant, last_seen_ts, batch_hint, ttl, affinity_key
- Evaluate routing policy per-request and pick candidate runtime/variant
- Execute fallback policy when selected instance is overloaded or unhealthy
- Emit routing decision traces to observability pipeline

Proposed API shapes (SDK + HTTP headers):
1) Create session (idempotent): POST /v1/sessions\body: { "owner": "user-123", "preferred_model": "redwood/ggml-7b-q5", "policy": "cost-safe" }
returns: { "session_id": "s_abc123", "assigned_variant": "ggml-7b-q5", "affinity_key": "hash:user-123" }

2) Attach to session: X-Session-Id: s_abc123  (header) or POST /v1/sessions/s_abc123/attach
3) Route decision (internal): Router consults session metadata + runtime health to pick instance and returns X-Runtime-Endpoint header on proxied request (transparent to client).

Session policy DSL (sketch):
- priority: [latency, cost, accuracy]   # ordered preference
- fallbacks: ["variant:fp16", "variant:int8", "variant:small-model"]
- batch_hint: { target_tokens: 32, max_delay_ms: 25 }
- cache_scope: [session, user, global]
- region_preference: [us-west-2, any]

Example policy JSON (for Console or SDK):
{
  "priority": ["latency", "cost"],
  "fallbacks": ["variant:fp16", "variant:int8", "variant:ggml-1.4b"],
  "batch_hint": { "target_tokens": 64, "max_delay_ms": 40 },
  "cache_scope": "session",
  "region_preference": ["us-west-2"]
}

Routing heuristics (notes):
- If session has active kv-cache on instance A and instance A has available capacity -> prefer A (sticky).
- If instance A overloaded -> consult fallbacks in-order, try variant on same instance before moving session to other instance (preserves KV locality).
- If instance A unhealthy -> promote session to a compatible instance in same AZ/region, mark cache as cold and emit higher-latency flag.
- For multi-tenant fairness, include a decay factor on absolute token throughput when satisfying affinity (so noisy heavy sessions can be bumped).

Fallback decision flow (pseudocode):
1) candidate = preferred_instance_for(session)
2) if candidate.has_capacity() -> return candidate
3) for v in session.policy.fallbacks:
     if candidate.can_serve_variant(v) and candidate.has_capacity_for(v):
         assign variant v on candidate and return candidate
4) search other instances in region for preferred_variant
5) if none, try other regions respecting region_preference
6) if still none, enqueue request to burst queue or return 503 with Retry-After and suggested variant list

Affinity metadata (fields to store in session store):
- session_id
- owner_id
- assigned_variant
- affinity_instance_id
- kv_cache_keyset_id
- last_seen_ts
- request_count / tokens_used (for decay logic)

Metrics to emit (routing):
- routing.latency_ms (decision time)
- routing.decision_type (sticky|fallback|reassigned)
- routing.fallback_reason (capacity|health|policy)
- routing.reassignment_count
- session.cache_hit_ratio (after assignment)
- session.tail_latency_95/99 (before and after reassignment)

Console UX thoughts (for later):
- Per-session view showing assigned instance, cache size, recent fallbacks, and ability to pin a session to a specific variant/instance (danger: manual pin could hurt autoscaling).
- Bulk policy editor for org-level defaults and per-application overrides.

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODO):
- How long to keep affinity after inactivity? (30m vs 24h) -> affects cold-start and storage footprint.
- Should router attempt cross-instance cache pre-warm (pull KV from origin) when reassigning? Costly but reduces latency.
- Atomicity: who owns cache consistency when variant changes? Some quantized variants have incompatible KV formats. Need conversion plan or forbid cross-variant reuse.
- Privacy: session metadata in session-store must be encrypted at rest; consider HSM/KMS tagging for Private deployments.

Implementation sketch (components):
- router service (stateless, but reads/writes session store)
- session store (redis cluster with TTL and ephemeral metrics)
- router health and scoring service (feeds best-candidate list)
- runtime agent endpoint that can accept pre-warm / transfer cache requests

Quick ascii diagram for reroute during fallback:

Client --> Router --> [Instance A (pref)] --(overloaded)-> Router -> [Instance B (fallback variant)] --> Model
                                         \n                                          --> Router logs fallback event

Short todo list (personal):
- [ ] prototype policy DSL parser and evaluator (ts or go)
- [ ] add simulated load test to verify sticky sessions reduce token cost by ~10-20% on chat patterns
- [ ] spike conversion/compatibility matrix for variant KV caches
- [ ] draft router telemetry schema and add to logs/metrics PR

Notes-to-self: keep this lightweight. Start with session-level variant selection and sticky-to-instance; add cross-instance cache transfer later as opt-in. Discuss with SRE about redis topology for session-store (hot keys).

References and inspiration:
- internal: GH-PR-1423 (sticky session prototype)
- external: "Serving at Scale" blog posts, prior work on memcached sticky shards

End of notes.
